subject.title: feat: add lease-bound metadata to session spawns

question: Should OpenClaw core own this named Agentic OS external-orchestrator protocol and snapshot state, or should core expose only a generic lease-authorized spawn seam for an external owner to implement?
rationale: The answer determines the durable public Gateway, storage, and ownership contract; it cannot be resolved safely by mechanically reshaping this contributor branch.

options.title: Adopt a generic core seam
options.body: Define the smallest owner-neutral authorization/spawn extension in core and move Agentic OS-specific RPC names, metadata, replay semantics, and storage to the downstream owner.

options.title: Sponsor the core protocol
options.body: Explicitly accept the Agentic OS methods and persistent state as a supported core Gateway contract, then require public API, migration, compatibility, and current-head live proof.

options.title: Keep it downstream-only
options.body: Decline a new core contract and let the downstream adapter use existing supported OpenClaw integration surfaces.

recommendation.title: Adopt a generic core seam
recommendation.body: Define the smallest owner-neutral authorization/spawn extension in core and move Agentic OS-specific RPC names, metadata, replay semantics, and storage to the downstream owner.

likelyOwner.reason: Likely routing point for the core-versus-extension architecture choice, though direct ownership history could not be verified in the constrained read-only environment.
